title: What if you breathed on top of Everest?
caption:
Teleported to Everest's summit, you'd faint within minutes. 🏔️🫁

The air up there is still about 21% oxygen, the same as at the beach.

But the summit air pressure is only about a third of sea level (≈253 vs 760 mmHg), so each breath brings roughly a third of the oxygen.

Without acclimatisation, useful consciousness at that altitude lasts only about 1–3 minutes (FAA hypoxia tables).

That's why climbers spend weeks adapting, and about 97% of Everest summits are made with bottled oxygen.

Send this to the friend who wants to climb Everest.

Tomorrow: toast on Venus.

⚠️ Don't try this. Climbing too high too fast can cause deadly altitude sickness.

#science #physics #whatif #sciencefacts #everest #biology #altitude #theimpossiblelab
sources: West JB et al. (1983) Barometric pressures at extreme altitudes on Mt. Everest: physiological significance. J Appl Physiol 54:1188-1194 (summit 253 Torr; inspired PO2 ≈43 Torr) https://air.unimi.it/bitstream/2434/176393/2/23-83JAP_Mount_Everest.pdf

FAA AC 61-107B CHG 1, Figure 2-3 Time of Useful Consciousness: 28,000 ft 2.5–3 min, 30,000 ft 1–2 min (TUC is not the onset of unconsciousness) https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_61-107B_CHG_1.pdf

NOVA/PBS Everest: rushed to 29,000 ft without acclimatising, 'we would become unconscious within a couple of minutes'; summit oxygen pressure about a third of sea level https://www.pbs.org/wgbh/nova/everest/exposure/higher.html

NZ Herald / Himalayan Database: about 3% of Everest summits without bottled oxygen (193 of 7,004 before May 2016) https://nzherald.co.nz/world/for-most-on-everest-bottled-oxygen-is-a-must-but-a-few-go-without/QKFZFPVDOU7SQGF4TGO26YLSWA
Sea-level inspired PO2 = 0.2093 × (760 − 47) ≈ 149 mmHg (standard alveolar gas equation); Everest height 8,848.86 m (2020 China–Nepal survey)
